translations.text: There was a certain man in the land of Ausitis whose name was Job. That man was truthful, blameless, righteous and God-fearing, and he kept himself apart and separate from every evil deed.
He had seven sons and three daughters.

His livestock was very great: seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred grazing she-asses, and a very great number of servants. His affairs were great on the earth. That man was a nobleman among the people of the east.
His sons would gather together with one another and hold a feast day after day. They would also bring their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

When the days of their drinking were over, Job would send for them and purify them. He would rise at dawn and offer sacrifices for them, one for each of them, and one calf for the sins of their souls, for Job said, "Perhaps evil has entered the minds of my sons against the Lord." Job did this every day.
Then came such a day, and the angels of God came to stand before God, and the devil also came and stood among them.
The Lord said to the devil, "Where do you come from?" The devil answered him, "I have gone around the whole earth and passed through everything under heaven, and now I am here."
The Lord said to him, "Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him on earth: a man who is innocent, truthful and God-fearing, and who keeps himself apart from every evil deed."
The devil answered before the Lord, "Does Job serve the Lord for nothing?
Have you not put a wall around him, around the inside of his house and around everything outside that belongs to him? Have you not blessed the works of his hands and made his livestock many?
But stretch out your hand and touch everything that he has, and see whether he will still bless you to your face."
Then the Lord said to the devil, "Here, I have given everything that belongs to him into your hands. Only do not touch him."
Then came such a day, when Job's sons and daughters were drinking in the house of their eldest brother.
And a messenger came to Job and said, "The yoked oxen were plowing, and the herd of she-asses was grazing near them.
Raiders came and carried them off, and they killed the servants with the sword. I alone escaped and came to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, "Fire fell from heaven and burned up all the sheep, and it devoured the shepherds as well. I alone escaped and came to tell you."

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, "The horsemen split into three bands, surrounded the camels and carried them off, and they killed the servants with the sword. I alone escaped and came to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking with their eldest brother.
Suddenly a great wind came from the desert and struck all four corners of the house. The house fell on your children and they died. I alone escaped and came to tell you."
Then Job rose up, tore his clothes and shaved the hair of his head. He fell to the ground, then rose and worshipped the Lord with his face to the ground.

And he said: "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I shall return there, to the earth. The Lord gave to me, and the Lord has taken from me. As he willed, so it was done. Blessed be the name of the Lord."
In all that happened to him, Job did not sin at all before the Lord, and he said nothing foolish against God.
And there came such a day, and the angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord,

and the devil also was among them. And the Lord said to the devil: "Where do you come from?" Then the devil said before the Lord: "I have passed through the earth beneath heaven and gone all around it, and now I am before you."

The Lord said to him: "Have you now seen my servant Job? For there is no one like him on earth: a man blameless and true, who serves God, keeps himself apart, and turns away from every evil deed. He still holds on to his innocence, yet you told me to destroy his possessions for nothing."
The devil answered and said to the Lord: "Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has for his own life.
But now stretch out your hand and touch his bones and his flesh, and see whether he will openly bow down to you, or rather bless you."
And the Lord said to the devil: "Behold, I give him over to you. Only spare his life."
And the devil went out from the Lord and struck Job with an evil sore from his feet to his head, and covered him with [?].
And Job took a potsherd to scrape away the pus, and he sat down on the dung heaps outside the city.
And when much time had passed, his wife said to him: "How long will you endure and say,
'Behold, I will wait a little while longer, and the hope of my salvation will come'?
Behold, your memory has perished from the earth: your sons and daughters, the pains and labor of my womb, for whom I wore myself out with toil for nothing.
And there you sit in the stench of worms, spending your nights in the open air,

while I, a wanderer and your servant, go from place to place and from house to house, waiting for the sun to set so that I may rest from my labors and from the pains that have surrounded me. But now say [?] a word against the Lord, and die."

But Job looked at her and said: "You speak like one of the foolish women. If we have received good from the hand of the Lord, shall we not endure this evil?" In all that happened to him, Job did not sin with his lips before the Lord.

And when his three friends heard of all this evil that had come upon him, each of them came from his own land to see what had happened to him: Eliphaz, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans. They came to him together to comfort him and to see him.
When they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. They cried out in a loud voice and wept. Each of them tore his own garment, and they threw dust on their heads.
And they sat with him for seven days and seven nights, and none of them said anything, because they saw that his wound was evil and very great.
After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his days,
and he said:
"Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night on which they said, 'It is a boy.'
Let that night be darkness. Let the Lord above not seek it out, and let no light come upon it.
Let darkness and the shadow of death seize it.
Let it not be a day of the year, nor let it be counted among the days of the months.
But let that night be in pain, and let no joy come upon it, nor any gladness.
But let him curse it who curses that day, he who is about to lay hands on the great sea-monster.
Let the stars of that night be darkened, and let it not last, nor come to light, and let it not see the morning star rising.
For it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb, and so take pain away from my eyes.
Why did I not die in the womb itself? When I came out of the womb, why did I not perish at once?
Or why did the knees of those who raised me receive me, or why did breasts nurse me?
Now I would be lying down and at rest; I would have slept and been at rest
with kings, the counsellors of the earth, who made a clamour with their swords,
or with rulers who had much gold, who filled their houses with silver;
or like a stillborn child that comes out of the womb, or like infants who have not seen the light.
There the ungodly burned out the anger of their wrath; there those weary in body have found rest.
All together, those of ages past do not hear the voice of the tax collector.
Small and great are there, and the servant of his own master.
Why then is light given to the embittered, and life to souls that are in pain?
They long for death and do not reach it, and they seek it as if it were treasure,
and they would rejoice when they reached it.
For death is rest for a man, and God has hemmed them in.
My sighs come before my food. I weep with fear.
For the fear that troubled me has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me.
I was not at peace, nor at quiet, nor do I have rest, and wrath has come upon me.
Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said to him:
Have these things perhaps been said to you many times? Who can bear the burden of these words of yours?
And if you have instructed many and given comfort to the hands of the weak,
and raised up the sick and given healing to weak knees,
But now pain has come upon you and has touched you, and you were thrown into haste.
Is not this fear of yours from folly, along with your hope and the wickedness of your ways?
Now remember: who was ever holy and perished? Or when and where were the truthful torn up by the root?
As I have seen, those who plow what is improper, and those who sow it, will reap pain.
By the command of the Lord they will perish, and by the breath of his wrath they will be destroyed.
The strength of the lion, the voice of the lioness and the roaring of the dragons were quenched.
The ant-lion perished, because it had no food. The lion's cubs abandoned one another.
If there had been any true word in what you said, no evil would have happened to you. Now is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge?
With fear and groaning in the night, fear falls upon people.
Dread and fear came upon me, and they made my bones tremble greatly.
And a spirit came before my face. My hair and my flesh shuddered.
And I arose, and there was no form before my eyes, but I heard only a breeze and a voice.
What now? Can a man be holy before the Lord, or can a man be blameless in his deeds?
Or does he not trust his own servants, and has he charged his angels with something perverse?
But those who live in houses of clay, we who are made of that same clay — how often has he crushed them like a moth?
And between dawn and evening they are no more, for they could not help themselves, and they perished.
He blew on them and they withered and perished, because they had no wisdom.
Call out, then, and see if anyone will answer you, or if you will see any of the holy angels.
For wrath kills the foolish man, and envy puts to death the one who has gone astray.
I have seen fools whose roots had spread out, but their provisions were suddenly devoured.
Their roots were cut off far from life, and they were tormented at the doors of those lower than themselves [?], and there was no one to rescue them.
For the righteous will eat what they gathered, and they will not be rescued from evil; their strength will be drained away.
For darkness does not come out of the earth, nor does pain sprout from the mountains,
but man is born to pain, just as the heron's chicks fly high.
Not so; but I would pray to the Lord God, and I would call upon the Lord God Almighty,
who has made great and unsearchable things, glorious and wonderful, beyond number;
who gives rain upon the earth and sends water under heaven;
who makes the lowly high and raises up those who have perished,
he brings to nothing the counsels of the gentiles, and their hands do not accomplish truth.
For he overtakes the wise in their cleverness, and he brings to nothing the counsel of those who devise many schemes.
By day darkness will come upon them, and at noon they will grope as at midnight.
Let them perish in battle; the weak one has escaped from the hand of the mighty.
Let there be hope for the weak, and let the mouth of the liar be stopped.
But blessed is the man whom the Lord has rebuked; do not turn away from the instruction of the Almighty,
for he rebukes and then restores again; he struck, and his hands will heal.
Six times he will deliver you from evil, and in the seventh evil will not touch you.
From famine and from death he will deliver you; in battle he will set you free from the hand of the sword.
He will shelter you from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear the evil that is coming.
You will scorn the false and the lawless, and you will not be afraid of wild beasts.
For the wild beasts will be at peace with you.
Then you will know that there is provision [lit. labour] in your house, and the order of your dwelling-house will not fail [lit. will not sin].
Then you will know that your descendants are many and your children like all the grass of the field.
And you will go to the grave like wheat in its season, reaped at its proper time, or like a sheaf on the threshing floor, gathered in due season.
Behold, thus we have searched it out, and this is what we have heard; but you, know for yourself what you have done.
Job answered and said:
If only someone would weigh my wrath and my pains and lift them together on a scale,
they would be found heavier than the sand of the seashore. But, as it seems, my words are evil.
For the arrows of the Lord are [?] (lit. 'weighed out') in my flesh; their fury drains my blood. When I begin to speak, they pierce me.
What then is it? Does the wild ass bray for nothing? No, it is looking for food. Or if the ox lets out its voice at the manger, what food does it have before it?
Or will bread be eaten [without?] salt [lit. 'bread of salt']? Or is there any taste in empty words?
For my soul cannot be at rest. I find my food foul-smelling, like the stench of a lion.
If only the Lord would grant it to me, and my request would come, and God would grant me what I hope for!
The Lord has begun, and he has wounded me. Let him not kill me outright.
Let this city, on whose walls I used to walk, be a grave for me. I will not hold back, for I have not been false to the holy words of my God.
What strength do I have, that I should endure? Or how long is my time, that my soul should bear it?
Is my strength the strength of stone? Or is my flesh made of bronze?
Or did I not trust in him? My help comes from him, yet my strength has left me.
His mercy has rejected me, and the Lord's care has disregarded me.
My neighbours did not look at me. I have run dry like a torrent-bed, and I have passed away like a wave.
Those who used to fear me now rush upon me, like snow or frozen ice
that melts from the heat, and no one can tell where it was.
So I too have been abandoned by all. I have perished and been driven out of my house.
Look at the roads of the Temanites and the paths of the Heshbonites [?], who border on them.
Those who trust in cities and riches have also become liable to shame.
But now you have become utterly merciless toward me, when you should have seen this wound of mine and been afraid.
Now what then? Am I asking anything of you, or do I need any of your strength,
for you to rescue me from the hands of my enemies, or deliver me from the hand of the mighty?
Teach me and I will be silent. If I have gone wrong in anything, tell me.
But words of truth are treated as vain things. It is not that I ask any strength from you.
Your rebuking words will not calm me, and I will not put up with what you have said.
Except this: you come at me as at an orphan, and you attack your friend.
Now look, I will face you, and I will not lie.
Sit down, and let there be no falsehood. Then join yourselves to justice again,
for there is no falsehood on my tongue. Or is my palate not trained in understanding?
Now is not a person's life on earth a trial, and his time like that of a hired day-labourer?
Or like a servant who fears his lord and trembles at his shadow, and like a hired worker who waits for his wages?
So I too have endured empty months, and nights of pain have been given to me.
When I lie down, I say, “When will it be morning?” And when I get up, I say again, “When will it be evening?” For I am filled with pain from evening until dawn.
My flesh is soaked with the filth of worms; I dissolve the clods of the earth as I scrape away the pus.
My life is slighter than a word spoken; it has perished in vain hope.
Remember, then, that this life of mine is a breath, and my eye will never again see good.
My eye will not look on me to see me. Your eyes are on me, and I am no more.
It is like a cloud that is cleared from the sky: if a person goes down to hell, he will not come up again.
He will not return to his house, and his place will not know him any more.
So now I will not hold back my mouth. I will speak, because I am in anguish. I will open my mouth in the bitterness of my soul.
Am I the sea, then, or a sea monster, that you have set a guard over me?
I said, “My bed will comfort me,” and on my couch I took up words to myself, by myself.
You frighten me in my sleep and wound me with visions.
You separate my breath from my soul, and my bones by death.
I will not live forever, that I should endure this. Leave me alone, for my life is in vain.
What is a human being, that you have made him great? Or why do you concern yourself with his mind?
Or will you watch over him until morning and bring him to rest?
How long will you not let me go, or give me a moment's peace? How long until I swallow my spittle in pain?
If I have sinned, what can I do to you, you who know the minds of human beings? Why have you made me a petitioner before you, so that I am a burden to you?
Or why did you not forget my lawless deeds and cleanse my sins? Now I am going back to the earth, and by morning I will be no more.
Bildad the Shuhite answered him and said:
How long will you speak like this, with a spirit full of words coming out of your mouth?
Will the Lord judge with partiality? Or will he who created all things pervert justice?
If your sons sinned before him, he gave them over to the power of their lawlessness.
But rise early and turn to the Lord Almighty in prayer.
If you were pure and true, he will hear your supplication and restore to you the fruit of righteousness.
And your beginning will be small, but your latter end will be beyond counting.
Ask, then, the former generation, and search out the fathers from generation to generation,
for we are short-lived and do not know, for our life upon the earth is a shadow.
Will not these teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their heart?
Can the rush spring up without water, or can the sedge grow tall without being watered?
While it is still on its roots and cannot yet be cut, before all the green herbage is watered, it withers.
So now shall be the end of all who have forgotten the Lord, for the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
And their houses shall be without inhabitants; their houses shall be a spider's web.
And even if they make their houses firm, they shall not stand; even if they guard it, it shall not endure,
for it is moist before the sun, and from its rot its shoot comes forth.
It shall lie on a heap of stones and live among the pebbles.
If he swallows it up, the place will stand to deny it. Have you not seen such a thing?
For this is the overthrow of the ungodly, but out of the earth another springs up,
for the Lord will not cast away the blameless, but he will accept no gift of the ungodly.
And he will fill the mouths of the true with laughter, and their lips with praise.
But their enemies shall be clothed with shame, and the ungodly shall have no portion.
Job answered and said:
Truly I know that it is so. How then can a man be righteous before the Lord?
And even if he wishes to go to judgment with him, he will not listen to him, so that he cannot answer him one word out of his thousand.
For he is wise in mind, he is mighty and great. Who, then, has been stubborn before him and held out?
He who makes the mountains old, and they do not know it; who overturns them in wrath;
who shakes what is under heaven from its foundations, and its pillars totter;
who commands the sun and it does not rise, and sets a seal upon the stars;
who alone stretched out the heavens, and walks upon the sea as on dry land;
who made the Pleiades, the evening star, Arcturus and the treasuries of the south;
who has made great and unsearchable things, glorious and wonderful, beyond number.
If he passes over me, I will not see him; or if he passes by me, I will not even notice it.
If he turns away, who will turn him back? Or who will say to him, "What have you done?"
For he himself will turn away wrath, and by him the sea monsters under heaven are brought low.
If the Lord would hear me, or if he would judge my words,
even if I were righteous, he would not hear me; I would have to plead for his judgment.
If I called and he heard, I would not believe that he had heard me.
Let him not crush me with thick darkness, for he has bruised me many times for no reason.
He does not let me draw breath, for he has filled me with bitterness.
And since he is mighty in strength, who then could stand against his judgments?
And even if I am righteous, my mouth is lawless; and even if I am blameless, I will still be shown to be crooked.
Whether I have done something ungodly, I do not know in my soul; I know only that my life is taken away.
Therefore I said: wrath destroys the great and the mighty.
For the wicked perish by a strange death, for the righteous have become a laughingstock.
They are given into the hands of the ungodly; he covers the faces of its judges. If it is not he himself, who is it?
But my life is swifter than a runner; my days have fled away and have not seen good.
Or does a ship leave a track of its way, or an eagle in flight that is seeking food?
And even if I speak, I forget my words; I hang my head and sigh,
and I tremble in all my limbs. I know that you will not let me go unpunished.
And since I am ungodly, why did I not die?
Even if I wash myself with snow and cleanse myself with pure hands,
even then you have plunged me deep into filth. My own garment has loathed me.
For you are not a man like me, whom I could answer, so that we might come together for judgment.
If only there were someone to stand between us as mediator and to rebuke, someone who would hear the case between us!
Let him take his rod away from me, and do not let fear of him terrify me.
Then I would not be afraid but would speak, for I know of no such thing in myself.
Since I am so weary in my soul, in my distress I will pour out my words against him; I would speak in the bitterness of my soul, in grief.
And I will say to the Lord: Do not teach me ungodliness! Why have you judged me like this?
Is it good for you if I sin against you? For you have rejected the work of your hands and looked favourably on the counsel of the ungodly.
Do you see as a human being sees? Do you see the way a human being sees?
Is your life a human life? Are your years the years of a man?
For you have searched out my iniquities and tracked down my sins.
I know that I have not been ungodly, but who is there who can rescue me from your hands?
Your hands made me and formed me; and after this you turned around and struck me down.
Remember that you formed me out of clay, and you are turning me back into earth again.
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh, and you made me firm with bones and sinews.
You put life into me, and your care guarded my spirit.
I have these things from you, and I know that you can do all things and that nothing is impossible for you.
And if I sin, you watch me closely, and you do not leave me unpunished for my iniquity.
If I have been ungodly, woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I still cannot lift up my eyes, for I am full of disgrace.
And I am hunted like a lion to be killed, and you turn and torment me cruelly again.
You renew my trials against me, you are angry with me with great anger, and you bring ordeals upon me.
Why did you bring me out of my mother's womb? Why did I not die there before any eye saw me?
Then I would have been as though I had never existed. Why was I not carried straight from the womb to the grave?
Is the time of my life not short? Leave me alone, so that I may rest a little
before I go to the place from which I will not return,
to the land of eternal darkness, where there is no light and where human life cannot be seen.
Zophar the Minaean answered and said:
Shall the one who says much not also hear a word in reply? Or does the fluent speaker think he is righteous?
Blessed is the one born of women who lives but a short life! Do not be excessive in words, for there is no one to answer you.
Do not speak thus: "I am pure in my deeds and blameless before him."
But how would the Lord speak to you and open his lips with you?

Then he would declare to you the power of wisdom, for it would be twice as much as yours, and you would understand that what has befallen you from the Lord is deserved, for what you sinned against him.
Or have you found the track of the Lord, or have you reached the end of what the Almighty has made?
The heavens are high, and what can you do? Or what do you know of the things deeper than Hell?
Or of what is longer than the measure of the earth, or of the breadth of the sea?
If he overturns everything all at once, who will say to him, "What is this you have done?"
For he knows the deeds of the lawless; he has seen wrongdoing and has not overlooked it.
But man twists words in another way. Man born of woman is like the wild ass of the desert.
If you have made your heart pure and stretch out your hands toward him,
if there is any lawlessness in your hands, put it far away from you, and let no falsehood dwell in your dwelling.
And then your face will shine forth like pure water; you will strip off your filth and will not be afraid.
And you will forget your toils like waves that have passed by, and you will not tremble.
And your prayer will be like the morning star, and life will shine forth for you at midday.
And you will take heart that there is hope for you; out of the thoughts of your heart and out of anxiety, peace will appear to you.
You will rest, and no one will fight against you; he will turn them, and many will entreat you.
And life will fail them, for their hope is destruction, and the eyes of the ungodly will waste away.
Job answered and said:
Now you too are indeed men; or will wisdom come to an end with you?
For my heart too is like yours, and I am no more foolish than you.
For a righteous and blameless man has become an object of scorn,
for at an appointed time he was destined to be thrown down by others, and their houses to be plundered by the lawless.
But let no one who is wicked trust that he will be blameless, those who provoke the Lord to anger, as though there would be no judgment for them.
But ask the four-footed beasts whether they will tell you anything, or the birds of the sky whether they will make anything known to you;
speak to the earth, whether it will say anything; or else the fish of the sea will tell you.
Who among all these does not know that the hand of the Lord made all this?
Is not the life of every living creature in his hand, and the spirit of every human being?
For the mind tests words, and the palate knows the taste of food.
Wisdom is found among the aged, and knowledge in a long life.
From him come wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his.
If he tears down, who will build up? Or if he shuts people in, who else will open?
If he holds back the water, he dries up the earth; if he lets it loose, he destroys the earth all at once and overturns it.
From him come strength and power; knowledge and understanding are his.
He sends counselors away as captives and leaves the judges of the earth bewildered;
he seats kings on thrones and girds them with the belt of their strength;
he sends priests away as captives and overthrows the mighty of the earth.
He alters [?] the lips of the faithful, and he knows the understanding of the elders.
He pours dishonor on rulers and heals the lowly;
he reveals deep things out of darkness and brings them out into the light from the shadows of death;
he leads nations astray and lets them go; he brings out the sons of the tribes and leads them.
He alters [?] the hearts of the rulers of the earth and leads them astray on a way they did not know;
let them grope in darkness and not in light; let them stagger like drunk men.
Look, my eye has seen all this, and my ears have heard it.
I know as much as you know, and I have no less understanding than you.
Not only that, but I will speak to the Lord and argue my case before him, if he is willing.
[ხ̃ ?] But you are all false physicians and healers of evils.
If only you would keep silent! It would be counted to you as wisdom.
Hear the arguments of my mouth, and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
What is this? Do you not speak before the Lord, and plot deceit in his presence?
Or do you shrink back from me? You will become judges yourselves.
Would it be good for you if he should search you out too? Even if you do everything and attach yourselves to him,
he will surely find something lacking and rebuke you. And if in secret you have shown partiality [?],
will not his terror make you tremble? Will not fear of him fall upon you?
Your thoughts will become like ashes to you, and your bodies like clay.
Be silent, so that I may speak and find rest from the anger in my heart.
I will take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hands.
If the Mighty One lays hands on me, as he has already begun to do, I will still speak and argue my case before him.
And this will be my salvation, for deceit shall not come before him.
Hear my words, hear them! For I will tell you, if you will listen [?].
Behold, I have come near to my judgment; I know that I shall be shown to be in the right.
Who is my judge? For now I will be silent and breathe my last.
I must keep still, and then I will not hide from your face.
Take your hand away from me, and do not let fear of you terrify me.
Then call me, and I will hear you; speak to me, and I will give you an answer.
How many are my sins? Teach me: what are they?
Why do you hide yourself from me and count me as your enemy?
Are you afraid of a leaf stirred by the wind? Or do you set yourself against me, who am like straw carried off by the breeze?
For you write down every evil against me and surround me with the sins of my youth;
you have set my feet in the stocks, you have watched over all my deeds, and you have reached even to the soles of my feet,
which are wearing out like a wineskin, or like a garment eaten by moths.
For a human being born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath,
like a flower that blooms and then falls; he passes away like a shadow and does not remain.
Have you not called even him to account and brought him into judgment before you?
Who then will be pure from defilement? No one.
And even if his life on earth is only one day, and his months are numbered by him, you have set him a time, and he will not pass beyond it.
Turn away from him, so that he may rest and take pleasure in his life like a hired laborer.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it sprouts again, and its shoots do not fail.
And even if its root grows old in the earth, and its root falls on rock,
from the breath of water it will blossom again and put forth leaves like a newly planted shoot.
But a man, once he has died, has passed away; a man has fallen and will be no more.
For in time the sea runs low, and a river, once spoiled, dries up.
When a man has fallen asleep, he will not rise again; as long as the heavens still exist, they will not be clothed again, nor will they be woken from their sleep.
If only you would keep me in Hades and hide me until your wrath passes, and appoint me a time when you will remember me!
If a man dies, he shall live, for he has completed the days of his life. I will wait until I am born again.
And then you will call me, and I will listen to you. Do not cast away the work of your hands.
For you have counted my ways, and you have not forgotten any of my sins.
You have sealed up my iniquities in a bag, and you have taken note of whatever was done wrong unwillingly.
But a mountain will surely fall, and a rock will grow old and be worn away from its place.
The waters have worn the stones smooth, and great waters have washed away the soil of the earth; and you have destroyed the patience of man.
You drove him off completely, and he perished; you turned your face toward him and sent him away.
Even if his sons become many, he does not know it; or if they become few, he still does not know it.
And yet his flesh was in pain, and his soul mourned.
Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Now then, does a wise man give an answer from the understanding of the spirit, and fill himself with pain of the belly?
You rebuke with words that were not fitting, with words that are of no use.
And you have spoken such words before the Lord.
You are liable for the words of your mouth. You have not weighed the words of the mighty.
Let your own mouth condemn you, not I, and let your lips testify against you.
What then? Did you exist before men, or were you born before the mountains?
Were you the first to hear the command of the Lord? Or did wisdom come upon you alone?
What do you know that we do not know? Or what have you understood that we have not?
Among us there are old men, older than you, with more days than a father's father.
You are punished for only a few of the sins you committed, yet you speak loudly and beyond measure.
How did your heart dare it? What have your eyes seen?
For you have poured out your anger before the Lord and brought such words out of your mouth.
Who among men could be blameless? Or who born of a woman has ever been righteous?
If he does not trust even his holy ones, and heaven is not pure before him,
how much less a loathsome and impure man, who drinks falsehood like a drink.
I will tell you, so listen to me, and I will declare to you what I have seen,
what the wise have spoken, and did not hide from their fathers.
To them alone the land was given, and no foreign seed came upon it.
The whole life of the ungodly is spent in anxiety, and the Mighty One has given him a numbered count of years.
His fear is in his ears. Just when he thinks he is at peace, ruin will come upon him.
Let him not believe that he will return out of darkness, for He himself has commanded that he be handed over to the power of the sword.
He is set apart as food for vultures. He knows his own fate, that he is waiting to fall, and a day of darkness will terrify him.
Grief and distress will seize him, like a commander who falls while he stands at the head of his men.
For he lifted up his hands before the Lord and stiffened his neck before the Almighty,
and he behaved before him with insolence, behind the thickness of his armor,
for he covered his face with his fat and made a collar [?] of fat on his thighs.
Let him live in desolate cities and enter houses with no inhabitants, and what they have prepared, others will carry off.
He will not grow rich, his fruit will not last, and his shadow will not remain on the earth,
nor will he escape darkness. The scorching heat will wither his plant, and his flower will fall.
Let him not believe that he will endure, for emptiness will come back to him as emptiness.
His cuttings will perish before their time, and his shoot will not grow green.
And let them pick him off like an unripe grape before its time; may he fall like the blossom of the olive tree,
for death is the witness against the ungodly, and fire has burned up the houses of those who take bribes.
And he will conceive pain; emptiness upon emptiness will come upon him, and his belly will gather up deceit.
Job answered and said: I have heard many such things. Wicked comforters are you all.
What now? Is there any order in words of wind? Or what has troubled you, that you answer back?
I too would speak against you, if only your soul were in this state in place of my soul,
and then I would rush at you with words and shake my head at you.
May there be strength in my mouth, and I would not hold back the movement of my lips.
For if I speak, my wound will not stop paining me; and if I keep silent, how will I be wounded any less?
But now he has worn me out, bewildered and rotting as I am; you have seized me,
and my falsehoods have risen up against me; it has answered me back to my face.
He brought on his wrath and threw me down, and gnashed his teeth at me. He has nailed the arrows of trials into me;
he has pierced my eyes with the points of his arrows; he struck my knees with the sword, and together they rushed upon me.
The Lord has handed me over into the hands of the false one and has thrown me among the ungodly.
While I was at peace he ruined me; he seized me by my hair and tore me apart, and set me up like a target.
Spearmen surrounded me and pierced my kidneys; without pity they poured out my gall on the ground.
They threw me down, one fall on top of another; the mighty ran at me.
They sewed sackcloth onto my skin, and my strength has been extinguished on the ground.
My belly is burning from weeping, and the shadow of death is on my eyelids.
There was no falsehood in my hand; my prayer was pure.
O earth, do not cover over the blood of my flesh, and let there be no resting place for my cry.
And now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high.
May my prayer reach the Lord, and may my eyes shed tears before him.
Let there be a pleading for a man before the Lord, as a son of man pleads for his neighbor.
My numbered years have come, and I am going on the road by which I will never return.
I am perishing, my spirit carried off. I beg for burial, and I do not get it.
I toil and grow weary, and what am I to do?
For strangers have plundered my possessions. Who is this? Let him give me his hand!
For they have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore you will not exalt them.
He will announce a share of wickedness; his eyes are fixed upon his sons.
You have made me a byword among the nations, and I have become a laughingstock to them.
My eyes have been blinded by wrath; I am hemmed in on every side by everyone.
The truthful were amazed at these things. Let the righteous rise up against the lawless.
Let the faithful keep to his own way, and let the one who is pure of hands receive comfort.
Not so! But all of you, press forward [?] and come, for I find no truth among you.
My days have passed away in stench, and the membrane of my heart has burst.
I have turned night into day; light is near, before the face of darkness.
And even if I endure, Hades is my home, and my bed is spread in darkness.
I have called death my father, and corruption my mother and sister.
Where then is my hope? Or will I ever see my good?
Will they go down with me to Hades, or will we go down into the earth together?
Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: 2 How long will you not cease? Be silent, so that we too may speak.
Why are we silent before you like beasts?
And you have taken up wrath. What now? If you die, will the land under heaven be left without inhabitants? Or will the mountains be overturned from their foundations?
And the light of the ungodly will be put out. Or will fire not come upon them?
Their light will turn to darkness in their dwelling, and their light will be put out.
Carry off his fruit from them for the most helpless [?]; let their plans go astray.
Their foot has fallen into a snare, and they are entangled in a trap.
Let snares come upon him; let the thirsty overpower him.
His cord is hidden in the ground, and his trap is on the paths.
May pains surround him; may many snares come upon him; may he be given over to severe famine.
An astonishing fall has been prepared for him.
May his legs [?] be devoured; may death consume his beauty.
May healing depart from his dwellings; may distress and a royal accusation befall him.
May night inhabit his dwelling; may his fine things be sown with brimstone.
And below, his roots will dry up, and above, his fruit will fall off.
May the memory of him perish from the earth, and may his name not be before the face of others.
May they drive him out of the light into darkness,
and may he not be known among his people, nor his house be preserved under heaven; instead, strangers will live in what was his.
Those who come after will groan over him, and those who came before were astonished.
These are the houses of the false, and this is the place of those who do not know the Lord.
Job answered and said:
How long will you torment my soul and break me down with words?
Only know that the Lord has done this to me. You speak evil against me; you are not ashamed before me, and you attack me.
Yes, truly I have gone astray, and error remains with me,
and I spoke words that were not fitting, and my words go astray and are untimely.
Leave off, for you make yourselves great against me and come at me with reproaches.
Understand that it is the Lord, for he has done this, and he has raised his strongholds against me.
See, I laugh at your reproach and will not speak. I cry out, and there is no justice for me anywhere.
I am walled in all around and cannot get through; he has set darkness before my face.
And he has stripped my glory from me; he has taken the crown from my head.
He has torn me down on every side, and I am gone; he has cut down my hope like a tree,
and he has brought his wrath down harshly on me. He has treated me with contempt, as an enemy.
His trials came upon me all together; those lying in wait for me surrounded me on my paths.
My brothers have withdrawn from me; they acknowledged a stranger rather than me. My friends have become merciless toward me.
My neighbors counted me as nothing, and those who knew my name forgot me.
To the kinsmen of my house and to my servants I became a stranger.
I called my servant, and he did not listen to me. My mouth pleaded with him.
I pleaded with my wife. I called the sons of my concubines, begging them.
But they cast me off forever. When I rise up, they plot evil against me.
Those who knew me came to hate me, and those I loved have risen up against me.
My flesh has rotted inside my skin, and my bones are held in your teeth.
Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, my friends, for the hand of the Lord has struck me.
Why do you persecute me as the Lord does, and why can you not get enough of my flesh?
Who will let me write down my words and set them in books forever,
with a pen of iron and of lead, or carve them into rock?
I know that the one who will deliver me is eternal, and that from the earth
he will raise up my skin, which has endured these things. For these things have been done to me by the Lord,
things that I myself know, which my own eye has seen and no one else's. All of them have been fulfilled in my bosom.
If you say, "What shall we say before him?" and you have found the roots of the words in him,
then you too should be afraid because of what is hidden. For wrath will come upon the ungodly, and then they will know where their righteousness is.
Zophar the Minaean answered and said:
I did not expect you to answer like this. And you have not understood more than I have.
I will listen to the teaching that rebukes me, and the spirit of understanding will answer him.
Have you not known this from long ago, ever since man was made on the earth,
that the joy of the ungodly ends in an astonishing fall, and the gladness of the lawless is destruction,
even if his sacrifice reaches up to heaven and his offering comes near the clouds?
When he thinks that he is firmly established, then he will perish completely, and those who knew him will say, "Now where is he?"
Like a dream that has flown away, he could not be found. He flew away like a vision in the night.
The eye saw him, and then saw him no more, and his own place will not know him.
May the lesser ones destroy his children, and may his hands gather pain like fire.
His bones were filled with his youth, and they will lie down with him on the earth.
If wickedness tastes sweet in their mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.
He will not spare it or let it go, and he will hold it under his palate.
And they will not be able to help themselves. The venom of an asp is in his belly.
He will vomit up the wealth he gathered by falsehood; an angel will drag it out of his house.
May the fury of dragons suck him dry; may the tongue of a serpent kill him.
May he not see the milking of the herds, nor the produce of honey and butter.
In vain and to no purpose he toiled for wealth, of which he will get no taste, like tough gristle that is not chewed and not swallowed.
For he tore down the houses of many weak people; he seized their wages and did not pay them.
There is no rescue for his possessions; he will not be saved by his own desire.
Nothing is left of his food; therefore his prosperity will not flourish.

When he thinks he has reached completion, then he will be in distress, and every affliction will come upon him. 23 If he should somehow fill his belly, may the fury of wrath be sent upon him. May pain rain down upon him.
And he will not escape from the hand of the sword; may a bow of bronze wound him.
May an arrow pass through his heart; may the stars turn about in his dwellings; may terrors come upon him.
And may all darkness be upon him; may unquenchable fire consume him; may a stranger do evil to his house.
May heaven reveal his lawlessness. May the earth be reckoned against him.
May destruction drag away his house completely; may the day of wrath come upon him.
This is the portion of the ungodly man from the Lord, and the reward of all his deeds from the One who sees all.
Job answered and said:
Listen, listen to my words, so that this may not be the comfort you give me.
Bear with me and let me speak, if you will not mock me.
What now? Is this reproof of mine from a man? Or how could I not be angry?
Look at me and be amazed; put your hands over your mouth.
When I remember, I am alarmed, and pains take hold of my flesh.
Now why do the ungodly live and grow old in riches?
Their offspring are as they wish, their children before their eyes.
Their houses are full; they fear no one. There is no chastisement from the Lord among them.
Their cow has not miscarried; their pregnant one was delivered safely and did not fail.
They remain like everlasting sheep, and their children sing and play.
They have taken up the timbrel and the harp, and they rejoice at the sound of merrymaking.
For they have spent their days in good things, and in the rest of Hades they have fallen asleep.
He says to the Lord: Depart from us! I do not even wish to know your ways.
What profit is there that we should serve him? Or what gain that we should come to meet him?
For their good things were in their hands, and he does not look upon the deeds of the ungodly.
Yet it is not so, but the lamp of the ungodly too shall be put out, and destruction shall come upon them, and pain shall seize them because of wrath.
And they shall be like chaff before the wind, or like dust that the whirlwind carries away.
May his fruit fail his sons; may he repay them, and he shall know it.
May his eyes see his own slaughter, and may he not escape from God.
For his will was with him in his house, and the number of his days was cut off.
How then is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? And he himself judges murderers.
This one dies in the strength of his folly, for he was wholly in luxury and prosperity,
and his entrails were full of tears, and his marrow was spread out.
But this one died in bitterness of soul, having eaten nothing, not one good thing.
And together they fell asleep upon the earth, and stench covered them.
So I know you: you come against me boldly,
since you will say: Where is the house of the ruler, and where is the dwelling of the ungodly?
Ask those who pass by on the road, and their sign will not be strange to you.
For the wicked one is handed over to the day of destruction; they shall lead him to the day of his wrath.
Who will declare his way to his face, and what he has done? And who will repay him?
And he was brought to the grave, and he kept watch in the tomb.
The pebbles of the torrent-valley were sweet to him, and after him every man went, and before him came countless others.
How then do you comfort me with empty comfort? I have no rest from you.
Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said to him:
Now, is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge?
What gain, then, is it to the Lord if you were blameless in your deeds? Or what profit is it that you were upright in your ways?
Or will he bring a charge against you, rebuke you, and enter into judgment with you?
Now, are not your wicked deeds many, and your sins beyond counting?
You took pledges from your brothers for nothing, and you took the clothing away from the naked;
you gave no water to the thirsty to drink, but took bread away from the hungry;
you showed favor to some people, and made them settlers of the land;
you sent widows away empty-handed, and you did evil to orphans.
Now, therefore, snares have surrounded you, and an astonishing war has come upon you.
Your light has turned to darkness for you, and water has covered you in your sleep.
Or does not he who watches over the heights see, and has he not brought low those who behave insolently?
And you said: What does the Mighty One know? Or does he judge through the thick darkness?
A cloud is his covering, and no one has seen him; he walks around the circuit of the heavens.
Will you not keep to the ancient paths that righteous men walked,
those who were seized before their time? Their foundations are a flowing river.
They are the ones who say: What will the Lord do to us? Or what will the Almighty bring upon us?
Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things. The counsels of the ungodly are far from him.
The righteous saw it and laughed, and the blameless one scorned them,
for their strength was destroyed, and fire consumed what was left of them.
Be steadfast, then, if you will endure [?], so that your fruit may be among good things.
Receive words from his mouth, and gather his words into your heart.
If you turn back and humble yourself before the Lord, then you will put falsehoods far from your dwellings.
You will be established upon the earth, on a rock, like the torrent-bed of Ophir.
And the Almighty will be your helper against your enemies, and will bring you pure silver, refined by fire.
And then you will find boldness before the Lord, and you will lift up your eyes to heaven with gladness.
When you pray to him, he will hear you, and he will grant you to fulfil your prayers again.
And he will restore to you a dwelling of righteousness, and on your ways there will be light with you.
For you humbled yourself and said, "He was arrogant"; and he will save the one who is lowly of eye.
He will deliver the innocent, and you will be saved by your pure hands.
Job answered and said:
And now, behold, I myself know that my reproof comes from my own hands; and his hand has become heavy upon me, so that I groan.
Who then might know how I could find him and come all the way to him?
And [?]
[?] he would tell me.
And he would come upon me with great power, and then he would not call to me with words.
For truth and reproof come from him, and he would bring my judgement to completion.
And I go away worn out, and I am no more; but who knows his last things?
His left hand acted, and I could not stand firm; his right hand will touch me, and I will not see.
For he knew my ways, and he tested me like gold.
And I will go out by his commandment, for I have kept his ways and will not turn aside,
for I will not depart from his commands, for I have hidden his words in my bosom.
If he himself has judged so, who is there to answer him? And whatever he wishes, that he has done.
Therefore I have hastened toward him, and in his teaching I have taken thought for him.
On this account I will be hastened before his face; I will consider, and I will be anxious because of him.
The Lord has softened my heart, and the Almighty has given me haste.
I did not think that darkness would come upon me, and that gloom would cover what is before my face.
Why then have the times been forgotten by the Lord?
The ungodly have moved boundaries; they have carried off the flock together with its shepherd.
They have led away the orphan's donkey and taken the widow's ox as a pledge.
They have pushed the weak aside from the way of justice, and the meek of the earth have all hidden themselves together.
They have become like wild donkeys in the field. Their deeds have gone out against me. Bread was sweet to him, for the young ones.
They have reaped a field that was not theirs before its time. The weak worked the vineyards of the ungodly without wages.
They have made many lie down naked, without clothing, and have taken away the covering of their bodies.
They are soaked by the rain of the mountains, and because they had nothing to cover themselves, they took shelter in the rocks.
They have snatched orphans from the breast and humbled the fallen.
They have wrongfully made them lie down naked, and they have taken bread from the hungry.
In narrow places they lay in wait with deceit, and they did not know the way of the righteous.
Those whom they drove out of cities and houses, the souls of infants groaned loudly.
Why did he himself not look upon them? While they were on the earth they did not understand, and they did not know the ways of justice, nor did they walk in its paths.
He knew their deeds and handed them over to darkness. And by night let him be like a thief.
The eye of the adulterer will watch for darkness. They said: "No eye will see me," for he has put a covering over his face.
By night he dug through the wall of a house. By day they sealed themselves in. They did not know the light,
for the shadow of death came upon all of them together at dawn.
He is feeble before the face of the water. Cursed be their portion on the earth; may their plant be seen
withered on the earth, for they have snatched the orphan's armful.
Therefore their sins were remembered, and they vanished like mist in the wind. Let what they did be paid back to them. Let every liar be broken like a tree, beyond healing,
for they did no good to the barren woman, and they had no pity on the one without a spouse.
In anger he overthrew the weak. If he rises again, let him not trust in his life.
When he falls ill, let him not hope to live, but let them fall by sickness,
for his pride has done evil to many. He has withered like mallow in the heat, and like an ear of grain that falls from its stalk by itself.
If that is not so, is there anyone who will say that I spoke this falsely and will make my words worthless?
Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
What, then, is the prelude, or the fear that comes from him who has made all things entirely in the heights?
Let no one suppose that there is any respite from trials. Upon whom does such an ambush from him not come?
How, then, could a man be righteous before the Lord? Or who that is born of women could make himself pure?
If he commands the moon, it does not shine, and the stars are not pure before him;
how much less a man, who is rottenness, and a son of man, who is a worm.
Job answered and said:
Whose side are you on, or whom do you mean to help? Is it not him who is strong, with great power and a mighty arm?
Or whom have you counselled? Is it not him from whom all wisdom comes? Or whom will you follow? Is it not him from whom the greatness of power comes?
To whom have you spoken these words? Whose is that breath that goes out from you?
Will not the giants drive [?] me beneath the waters and their neighbours?
Hell is naked before him, and destruction has no covering.
He stretches out the north over nothing and has hung the earth upon nothing at all.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the clouds do not burst beneath them.
He holds the face of the throne and spreads his clouds over it.
By his command he has drawn a circle on the face of the water, as far as the end of light and darkness.
And the pillars of heaven flew up and were astonished at his rebuke.
By his power he calmed the sea, and by his knowledge the waves are broken.
And the bars of heaven fear him; by his command he killed the apostate dragon.
Behold, these are only parts of his ways, and beyond this I shall hear in him the depth of his words. And the power of his thunder, who knows when he will use it?
Then Job continued his discourse and said:
As the Lord lives, who has judged me in this way, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
as long as this breath is still in me, and the divine spirit that is in my nostrils,
my lips shall not speak lawlessness, and my soul shall not speak falsehood.
Far be it from me to declare you right as long as I live, for I will not give up my innocence.
I hold fast to righteousness and will not let it go, for I do not know of myself that I have done any lawless deed.
Not so; rather, may my enemies be like the overthrow of the ungodly, and those who have risen up against me like the destruction of the lawless.
And what is the hope of the ungodly, that he holds on so stubbornly? If he trusts in the Lord, will he be saved?
Or will the Lord hear his prayer? Or when distress comes upon him,
will he have any boldness before him? Or if he calls upon him, will he hear him?
But now I will tell you what is in the hand of the Lord, and I will not lie about what is with the Almighty.
Behold, you all know that you assail me idly and in vain.
This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the reward of the mighty will come upon them from the Almighty.
And if their sons multiply, they will be given over to slaughter; or if they grow up, they will become beggars for bread; and those who are still alive will be finished off by death.
No one will have mercy on their widow.
And if he gathers silver like earth, and gathers gold like clay,
the righteous will gather all of this, and the truthful will take possession of their wealth.
And his house has become like a moth and like a spider.
The rich man has lain down and will do so no more; he has opened his eyes, and he is no more.
For pains have come upon him like waters, and by night a mist has carried him away.
Burning heat will take him up and carry him off, and will scatter him from his place.
And it will fall upon them and will not spare; he will flee headlong from its hand.
And he will clap his hands at him and carry him away from his place.
For there is a place for silver, from which it comes, and a place for gold, from which it comes forth,
for iron comes from the earth, and bronze is hewn out like stone.
He has set an order for darkness, and he will search out every end: the stone of darkness and the shadow of death,
a ravine cut off by dust; but those who have forgotten the right ways have grown weak and are gone from among men.
Bread comes forth from the earth; beneath it, it is turned up like fire.
Its stones are the place of sapphire, and its dust is gold.
No bird has known its paths, and the eye of the vulture has not seen it.
The sons of the proud did not trample it, and the lion did not pass over it.
On the summits of the rock he stretched out his hands; he overturned the mountains from their foundations.
He broke open the hard places of the rivers; his eye saw every precious thing.
And he revealed the depths of the rivers and brought his power to light.
But wisdom, where is it found? Or which is the place of knowledge?
No one knows its way, nor is it found among people.
The abyss said, "It is not in me"; and the sea said, "It is not with me."
Enclosed treasure will not be given in its place, nor can silver equal it as its price.
Nor can the gold of Ophir equal it, nor onyx, carbuncle and sapphire.
Nor can gold and mani [?] equal it, nor vessels of gold in exchange for it.
The [?] and the lowly will not be remembered; but remember wisdom above the innermost things.
The topaz of India will not equal it, and it cannot be compared with pure gold.
But wisdom, where is it found? Or what is the place of understanding?
Every person has forgotten it, and it is hidden from the birds of the sky.
Destruction and death said, "We have heard of its excellence."
The Lord has firmly established its way, and he himself knows its place.
For he [looks upon] everything that is under heaven. He sees and knows all things, as many as he made on the earth,
when he made the balance of the winds and the measures [?] of the waters.
Thus he saw and counted them, and [made] a way with a clear voice.
Then he saw it and declared it; he prepared it, searched it out, and said to man: "Behold, the service of God is wisdom, and turning away from evil is knowledge."
Then Job continued again and said in a parable:
Who will make me as in the former months, and in those days when the Lord guarded me?
When his light shone over my head; when by his light I walked through darkness;
when I was greatly at ease in my ways; when the Lord took care of my house;
when I was very rich in righteousness, and my servants were around me;
when my paths flowed with butter and my mountains poured out milk;
when I went out early in the morning into the city, my seats were set out in the streets;
the young men saw me and hid themselves; all the old men rose up for me;
the princes stopped speaking and laid their hands on their mouths.
And those who heard me called me blessed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths;
for the ear that heard me called me blessed, and the eye that saw me turned aside;
for I rescued the poor man from the hands of the mighty, and I helped the orphan who had no helper;
the blessing of the one who was perishing came upon me, and the mouth of the widow blessed me;
I put on righteousness and adorned myself with justice like a garment;
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame;
for I was a father to the weak; I looked into the case that I did not know;
I broke the jaws of the deceitful and took the plunder out from between their teeth;
I said: "My life will grow old; like the trunk of a palm tree I will live for many years,
my roots will spread out over the waters, and the dew will settle on my harvest."
My glory became empty with me, and my bow is in my hands.
They listened to me and paid attention to me, and they fell silent at my counsel.
And they added nothing more to my words, and they were glad whenever I spoke to them.
Like thirsty ground that waits for the rain, so they waited for my words.
If I laughed with them, they could not believe it, and the light of my face did not fade.
I looked into their ways and sat as chief, and I dwelt like a king among the valiant, like one who comforts the afflicted.
But now, look, they laugh at me. Now, look, the very lowliest teach me a thing or two, whose fathers I despised, whom I did not count as equal to the dogs of my flocks.
And what is the strength of their hands to me? Their end has perished upon them.
They were in want and hunger, those who only yesterday fled into the waterless land from distress and misery,
who gathered herbs in the mountains, whose food was greens; without honour and despised, lacking every good thing, who even chewed the roots of trees because of their great hunger.
Thieves have risen up against me,
whose houses were the holes of the rocks.
They cried out among the shelters of the thickets [?], those who were raised among the brushwood [?] of the field;
children of fools and of the dishonoured, their name and renown [?] extinguished from the earth.
And now, behold, I am their lyre, and they hold me as a byword.
They loathed me and stood far away from me, and they did not hold back from spitting before my face.
He opened his quiver and afflicted me, and they put bridles on my face.
On the right hand of the young growth they have risen up. His foot was stretched out, and he made a way toward me to the places of his destruction.
My paths were broken up; he stripped my garment from me.
For he shot his arrows at me, and he does to me whatever he wishes; I am worn down in pains.
My pains return to me again. My hope has passed away like the wind, and my life like a cloud.
And now my soul has gone out of me. Days of pain have been given to me.
By night my bones are burned, and my sinews are loosened.
With great force he seized my garment; they closed around me like the collar of my tunic.
They counted me equal to clay; he set my portion with earth and ashes.
I cry out to you, and you do not hear me. They stood and examined me,
and they fell upon me without mercy; with a strong hand you torment me.
And you have set pains upon me, and you have cast me out of life.
I know that death will crush me, for the house of every mortal is the earth.
If only I were able to lay hands on myself, or if I could beg someone else and he would do this for me!
For I used to weep over all the weak, and I sighed when I saw a man in distress.
I waited for good, and behold, evil days came upon me.
